categories.name: Rules & Pieces
categories.blurb: How the pieces move and games end

questions.q: How many squares are on a chessboard?
questions.e: An eight by eight grid.

questions.q: How many pieces does each player start with?
questions.e: Eight pawns and eight other pieces.

questions.q: Which piece moves diagonally only?
questions.e: Each bishop stays on one colour all game.

questions.q: Which piece moves in an L shape and can jump over others?
questions.e: Two squares one way and one square across.

questions.q: What is castling?
o: A single move involving the king and a rook
questions.e: Neither piece may have moved and the path must be clear.

questions.q: What is stalemate?
o: The side to move has no legal move and is not in check
questions.e: Stalemate is scored as a draw.

questions.q: What happens when a pawn reaches the far rank?
o: It is promoted to another piece
questions.e: Almost always promoted to a queen.

questions.q: What is en passant?
o: A special pawn capture of a pawn that has just moved two squares
questions.e: It must be played immediately or the right is lost.

categories.name: Openings & Ideas
categories.blurb: The theory behind the first moves

questions.q: Which opening begins with the moves 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5?
questions.e: Also called the Spanish Game.

questions.q: Which defence answers 1.e4 with 1...c5?
questions.e: It is the most popular reply to 1.e4 at top level.

questions.q: What is the Queen's Gambit?
o: 1.d4 d5 2.c4, offering a pawn for central control
questions.e: Black can accept or decline the pawn.

questions.q: What is a fork?
o: One piece attacking two or more enemy pieces at once
questions.e: Knights are especially good at forking.

questions.q: What is a pin?
o: A piece cannot move because a more valuable one sits behind it
questions.e: An absolute pin is against the king.

questions.q: How many points is a queen worth in the standard material count?
questions.e: Rook five, bishop and knight three, pawn one.

questions.q: What is zugzwang?
o: Being forced to move and worsen your own position
questions.e: Common in king and pawn endgames.

questions.q: What is the fastest possible checkmate, delivered by Black?
questions.e: It requires very poor play by White.

categories.name: Champions & History
categories.blurb: The world title through the years

questions.q: Who was the first official world chess champion?
questions.e: He took the title in 1886.

questions.q: Which American won the world title in 1972?
questions.e: He beat Boris Spassky in Reykjavik.

questions.q: Which Soviet champion held the title from 1985 into the 1990s?
questions.e: He became the youngest champion at 22.

questions.q: Which computer beat Garry Kasparov in a 1997 match?
questions.e: IBM's machine won the six-game rematch.

questions.q: Which Norwegian became world champion in 2013?
questions.e: He beat Viswanathan Anand in Chennai.

questions.q: Which Indian player was world champion from 2007 to 2013?
questions.e: He held titles in classical, rapid and blitz.

questions.q: Which body governs international chess?
questions.e: The Federation Internationale des Echecs, founded in 1924.

questions.q: What is the highest title FIDE awards?
questions.e: It requires norms and a rating threshold.
